body:
**Why.** Speed: every builder's gate runs the whole `lamp-voice` suite, and on a loaded host one timed test fails in almost every full run, a different one each time, each passing alone. Each such failure costs a rerun and a paragraph of explanation (the fourth builder's #698 comments of 2026-10-14; the first builder's runs of 2026-10-15). On the office Mac (x86_64, load average 6 to 7 with the other builders' sessions and a podman ARM64 build), serial (`--test-threads=1`), in three full runs:

| Run (2026-10-15) | Failed | Message | Alone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23:40 | `coordinator::tests::endpoint_session::complete_verdict_ends_early_but_resumed_speech_keeps_the_turn` | `physical privacy closed or lost freshness` | 5/5 |
| 00:00 | `coordinator::tests::pilot_faults::ring_fault_during_an_answer_keeps_the_conversation_and_cleans_up` | `service privacy freshness lost before next observation`, peer privacy gap 53261 us | 5/5 |
| 01:09 | `coordinator::tests::pilot_faults::sigterm_while_the_failure_notice_plays_stops_cleanly` | `service privacy freshness lost before next observation`, peer privacy gap 6543 us | 5/5 |

All three are the privacy-freshness bound being missed by a test's real worker processes when the host is slow, not a fault in what each test checks.

**Wanted.** Find the bound these tests rely on (the privacy peer's freshness, `crates/voice/src/transport.rs` and the coordinator's privacy observation), and make the tests deterministic on a loaded host without loosening what production enforces: a test clock, or a test-only freshness bound passed in, or the test's own wait for readiness. Show the three passing in ten full serial runs on the Mac while a podman ARM64 build runs beside them, and the native ARM64 CI green.

**Hand back.** The change and the ten runs. One pull request (`fourth-P1`). After #698.

**Most likely wrong.** That production's bound is right for the lamp under load too: if a test misses it at 53 ms, the lamp at 74 °C with the eyes and the voice may as well. Say so if the numbers suggest it.

comments.body: First builder, 02:13: scope widened. Also the motor supervisor's fixtures that fail on a loaded host at `motor/tests.rs:441` (`owned child timed out: None`), five in the third builder's gate of 2026-10-15 (crash/stalled-control, explicit-current-segment, failed-reap, frozen-config/executable, idle-ready; evidence linked on #709), each passing alone. Same aim: deterministic on a loaded host, production bounds unchanged.

First builder, 02:23: a fourth of the same kind in the full serial run at 02:22: `coordinator::tests::early_end::a_lone_lamp_and_a_pause_and_the_question_go_as_one_request`, `physical privacy closed or lost freshness`, the last record `privacy worker did not stop within shared 300 ms deadline; forced termination required; reaped with signal: 9`. Passes alone 5/5.

Fourth, 02:55 ICT: first loaded qualification failed (1,051/2/6,21 suites, 509.801 s). Original three and all motor cases passed; adjacent endpoint `a_complete_verdict_ends_at_one_second_and_its_answer_plays` and pilot `failure_notice_yields_mid_play_to_a_new_owner_under_vad_only` failed privacy freshness. Two overlapping real ARM64 cross-build cycles passed. This is the Intel Mac/x86_64 Podman VM, not a lamp. Failed source and raw evidence are being pushed on lamp-fourth; no rerun to hide the failure. Extending the same stepped peers to these scripted cases and incorporating the additional early-end case.

Scope question for the assigned motor fixtures: may Fourth add a narrow injected-clock seam to `crates/body/src/runtime/supervisor.rs`? Concretely, `Supervisor<C = SystemClock>` retains all current production constructors on SystemClock, adds an explicit clock constructor, and preserves every bound. Worker/core already accept a clock. A test-only sequenced Step/Ack channel then keeps parent, child, actual control/data FIFO and original evidence timestamps in one domain, with real startup/exit watchdogs and actual reap proof. Today the gate_segment fixture blocks child control handling while the parent's real20ms inhibit deadline runs; assertions/filesystem work can consume that deadline, and Supervisor enforces before draining receipts. Preflight alone cannot eliminate this race. Body belongs to Fifth, so I have not changed it; Voice work continues while this scope question waits.

Pushed evidence: https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/8bbf10b879134d0c9217ce8f9403dd0c35d504fb/lampOS/docs/verification/voice-fixtures-loaded-v1-20261015/README.md

Fourth, 03:34 ICT: v2 completed two full serial Mac passes (each 1,073/0/6,21 suites), then failed run 3 (1,072/1/6) in `endpoint_session::hung_worker_never_delays_capture_endpoint_or_session_end`: `capture discontinuity`. All originally named cases and motor cases passed in all three. Nine overlapping ARM64 cross-build cycles passed. The failed source, full raw output, counts and load samples are [retained on lamp-fourth](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/0a89d2ea46d08e0e835a80668ba6b3ecb8ba0564/lampOS/docs/verification/voice-fixtures-loaded-v2-20261015/README.md); this is the Intel Mac/x86_64 Podman VM, not a lamp.

The endpoint synthetic capture source currently timestamps overdue 10 ms blocks when the thread sends them, so a scheduler pause can appear as a source discontinuity. The failed block's actual delay was not recorded; this is inferred from the source. Correcting the fixture to retain its immutable scheduled acquisition times, with real process/envelope clocks and unchanged 100 ms stale refusal. New focused checks also prove clock callback errors and watchdog expiry retain cleanup ability. No production bound or Body source has changed.

V3 is retained as a failed qualification: the first full serial Mac run passed 1,077 / 0 / 6 ignored; the second ended 1,076 / 1 / 6 with `early_end::an_answer_with_nothing_said_before_the_lamp_is_sure_is_never_played` losing privacy freshness. Six overlapping release ARM64 cross-build cycles passed. This is the Intel Mac plus its x86_64 Podman VM, not lamp or native ARM64 execution.

[Raw runs, source identity, counts, load samples and failure](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/tree/db59f2db129f35467f023c03c6ee929c6a8c235f/lampOS/docs/verification/voice-fixtures-loaded-v3-20261015). No source changed during qualification. The original selected lone-name case, all endpoint scenarios and all motor scenarios passed both runs. Exact privacy-consumption age is not inferred from the error.

The shared real-provider EarlyEnd fixture now explicitly selects the existing test-only bounded tolerance for all ten coordinator scenarios/eleven conversations, waits for actual provider Ready before starting producers, and preserves scheduled source acquisition times. Its focused gate passed 13 / 0 / 0; a background service-send diagnostic is being reviewed before the next frozen full run. Production and unrelated tests retain 50 ms. The Body clock-seam ownership question remains pending; no Body edits. Ready for lamp-voice: no.
